multiply/pair: The dot product takes two vectors of the same length, here w and x, and gives back a single number.
multiply/mult: First, multiply matching entries: two times one is two, minus one times four is minus four, and three times two is six.
multiply/add: Then add up the products: two, minus four and six make four. That sum is written w dot x, read “w dot x”.
multiply/formula: In symbols, w dot x is the sum over i of w i times x i. w i is entry i of w, the same as w of i, and the big sigma, a Greek capital S, means add up what follows for every position i.
multiply/weigh: Read w as weights: each entry of x counts as much as its weight says, and a negative weight makes it count against.
sign/arrows: In two dimensions, picture each vector as an arrow from the origin. Here w is the arrow to the point two, one.
sign/same: When x points roughly the same way, like three, one, the products agree, and the dot product is positive: seven.
sign/perp: Turn x to minus one, two, at a right angle to w, and the products cancel: minus two plus two is zero.
sign/opp: Turn it further, to minus two, minus one, and the dot product goes negative: minus five.
sign/agree: So the sign says whether two vectors agree: positive when they point the same way, zero at a right angle, negative when they point apart.
solve/p1: The dot product also runs backwards. w is two, one, three, and x is one, a, two, where a stands for a missing entry. w dot x is ten. What is a?
solve/known: Multiply the pairs you know: two times one is two, and three times two is six. Together, eight.
solve/a1: The middle pair, one times a, makes up the rest: ten minus eight, two. So a is two.
solve/p2: Now w is three, two, one, x is one, a, four, and w dot x is thirteen.
solve/k2: The known pairs give three and four: seven. So two times a is thirteen minus seven, six.
solve/a2: Divide by the weight, two: a is three.
